source: Durian Orchard (ការដាំធូរេន), by Vann Thana Busab and Montry Vong Phanith, published by the Northwest Cambodia Provinces Fruit Culture Development Committee (Battambang), 1998, 59pp, AIDOC code 178-001
text: The source includes a short section on abnormal, non-infectious durian tree symptoms -- physiological problems rather than pest or disease damage -- such as leaf yellowing/scorch from nutrient imbalance or water stress, fruit that develops with uneven or empty (unfilled) segments due to poor pollination, and premature fruit drop linked to sudden water stress or over-fertilizing with nitrogen close to fruit-set. Because the scanned page images for this section were faint in places, growers are advised to treat this as a general pointer that such physiological problems exist and are usually traceable to a water, nutrition, or pollination cause, rather than as a definitive diagnostic guide; a specific unexplained abnormality should be checked with a local agricultural extension officer.
